$schema_note: Machine-readable source of truth for docs/DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md. scripts/release.sh reads this file. If you change a release's scope here, update DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md's table in the same commit -- they must never silently diverge.

releases.theme: Platform Bootstrap (prerequisite, not a customer-facing release)

backend.note: versioned event schemas + OpenAPI contracts + common libs

load_test.focus: Nothing deployed yet -- no service exists to load test.

releases.milestone: A hello-world service can be scaffolded, built, containerized, and deployed to a local/staging k8s cluster via the shared pipeline.
top_mistakes: Letting kart-shared become a dumping ground for domain logic instead of only versioned contracts + generic libs (PLATFORM_BLUEPRINT.md §2.2 item 3)
Hardcoding CI steps per service instead of calling kart-devops's reusable workflow_call -- guarantees drift across 18 repos later
Skipping branch protection / required PR review on kart-shared's main -- it is the one repo every other repo depends on as a package

frontend: Auth flows (login/register/MFA/SSO/password-reset) in kart-web and kart-admin-web
Category navigation (mocked, then wired to real endpoint)

load_test.focus: Identity sits on every authenticated request path platform-wide -- this is not optional even at MVP scale.

releases.milestone: A user can register/log in; site navigation renders real categories.
top_mistakes: Storing refresh tokens or session state in a way the API Gateway's revocation-list Redis check can't see (breaks logout/role-change/lock instantly)
Skipping the JIT-provisioning / external-IdP role-mapping edge cases -- these are resolved decisions in edge-cases.md, not open questions to improvise at code time
Treating MFA/SSO as a Phase 2 add-on and shipping password-only auth first -- BRD §24.2 already scopes it into this service, retrofitting RBAC later is expensive

frontend: PLP/PDP browsing (product cards, category pages wired to real data)

load_test.focus: Inventory is the platform's highest-contention service (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE hot path) -- give it the longest hardening runway now, don't defer to Release 5.

releases.milestone: Browse the full catalog with real stock status.
top_mistakes: Testing the oversell-prevention lock only at low concurrency -- the race only reproduces under real concurrent load, run the High-tier test before calling this release done
Forgetting the Product/Variant aggregate transaction-boundary split documented in ddd-model.md and collapsing them into one aggregate for convenience
Skipping the replenishment-racing-an-active-reservation edge case -- it's a named, resolved edge case, not a hypothetical

load_test.focus: Search (read-heavy, 20:1 read:write per BRD §4.4) and Offer's pricing-quote path (documented hot read path) both need Medium-tier verification before GA.

releases.milestone: Search works, prices/promos are real, users manage their profile.
top_mistakes: Cache-invalidating pricing/promo flags on a TTL instead of write-through (BRD §16 explicitly mandates write-through for price-sensitive data -- this exact mistake was caught and fixed once already in kart-offer-service's own edge-cases.md)
Reusing an expired PricingQuote snapshot across a slow checkout instead of enforcing its TTL
Rebuilding the Search index in place instead of blue-green -- a live reindex-in-place will serve inconsistent facets mid-rebuild

load_test.focus: Cart sits immediately upstream of the money path -- verify it holds up before Release 5 depends on it.

releases.milestone: The full pre-checkout shopping experience works end-to-end.
top_mistakes: Making the lazy stock/price validation gRPC call a hard gate on checkout initiation instead of fail-open with circuit breaker (architecture.md is explicit: never a hard gate)
Losing the sum-on-overlap / union-on-distinct cart-merge rule on login and silently picking one behavior
Forgetting the UserDataErased hard-delete responsibility for Cart and Wishlist (ADR-0016 names both directly) -- a GDPR gap here is a compliance bug, not a nice-to-have

releases.theme: Money Path: Checkout, Payment, Order Saga
releases.priority: highest-priority gate in the entire plan -- do not compress this release to hit a date

load_test.focus: Full Order Saga end-to-end (Order -> Inventory reserve -> Payment charge -> confirm) at High tier, then the full BRD §26 chaos suite (kill an Order pod mid-request, saturate RabbitMQ queue depth, introduce PostgreSQL replica lag, drop 20% inter-service packets), then an Extreme-tier flash-sale breaking-point test.

releases.milestone: MVP-complete: a customer can actually buy something, and the order-critical-path is hardened for flash-sale scale.
top_mistakes: Missing or incorrect Idempotency-Key handling on POST /payments/charge or POST /orders -- the single most expensive mistake on this path (double-charge / duplicate-order risk under client or gateway retry)

Treating the Saga as roll-forward-only and skipping the compensation path (Inventory release, Payment refund) -- test the failure flow (BRD §12.2) as thoroughly as the success flow (§12.1), not as an afterthought
Deploying Order before Payment's and Inventory's real contracts are live in the same environment, not just 'approved' on paper
Running the chaos suite against Production instead of Staging by accident -- confirm target environment before every chaos experiment
Calling this release done after only the happy-path load test -- the Extreme-tier breaking-point test is not optional here, it is the entire point of this release existing

load_test.focus: Notification is the platform's broadest fan-in consumer -- verify consumer autoscaling under full event fan-in volume, not just the happy path.

releases.milestone: Orders ship, track, and notify automatically.
top_mistakes: Skipping the DLQ/retry-tier verification for Notification's nine-plus consumed event types -- a silently-dropped notification is invisible until a customer complains
Not testing the carrier-webhook duplicate-delivery and out-of-order-delivery edge cases before going live (both are named, resolved edge cases in delivery-tracking-service)
Letting the per-carrier circuit breaker share a bulkhead with other carriers -- one carrier's outage should never degrade another carrier's shipments

load_test.focus: Explicitly verify Recommendation's fail-open degrade behavior under load -- its own architecture.md flags a distributed-monolith risk if this isn't tested, not just its happy path.

top_mistakes: Letting Recommendation's synchronous Inventory/Product availability-filter calls become a hard dependency instead of degrading gracefully on timeout
Missing the duplicate-review-submission-for-the-same-delivered-order edge case (named, resolved) and allowing double reviews
Racing a moderation rejection against an already-updated rating average without the documented resolution order

frontend: kart-admin-web full build-out: RBAC-gated dashboards, catalog/coupon/user-management consoles, analytics dashboards/funnels

load_test.focus: Analytics consumes every event published by every other service simultaneously (ADR-0004) -- this is the true full-fan-in stress test.

releases.milestone: Back office complete, full observability across the platform.
top_mistakes: Letting Admin own a parallel authorization/role table instead of consuming Identity-issued claims (this exact mistake was caught and fixed once already, see services/README.md's gap-closure table)
One of Admin's five synchronous fan-out dependencies (Product/Category/Offer/Identity/Inventory) missing its own independent circuit breaker, letting one dependency's outage cascade into another
Redacting PII in Analytics after ingestion instead of redact-in-place at the UserDataErased consumer -- a compliance gap, not a data-quality nice-to-have

releases.theme: GA Hardening (final release, no new services)
frontend: Remove all remaining feature flags platform-wide
kart-web Lighthouse / Core Web Vitals / SEO audit

load_test.focus: Full-system flash-sale simulation across the entire platform simultaneously (not just the Order path this time) + the full BRD §26 chaos suite run platform-wide.

top_mistakes: Leaving a stale feature flag in code past its feature's 100% rollout (api-strategy.md's own explicit rule: delete the same or next sprint)
Treating the full-system Extreme test as 'we already tested Order in Release 5' -- concurrent load across all 18 services surfaces cross-service resource contention no single-path test can

Skipping the security/pen-test pass because 'each service already passed its own Security Review gate' -- a system-wide pass catches cross-service auth/authorization gaps individual passes structurally can't see
